findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "complexity", "dominated").

findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's touching-endpoints note uses overlap in two senses without saying which test each problem uses, so it can be misread.
findings.evidence: [1,2],[2,3] overlaps for merge, not for rooms. / Use < when touching endpoints are allowed
findings.fix: Write one table: Problem | touching [1,2],[2,3] | operator. The rows are merge (merged, <=), rooms (no conflict, < or pop on <=) and balloons (overlap, one arrow).

findings.summary: The matched counter is named but never explained, so the O(1) slide is asserted rather than taught.
findings.evidence: "Track a matched counter; a slide touches only two slots" / "Each slide is O(1), not an array re-compare"
findings.fix: Add one line: matched counts the slots where window count equals pattern count. When a slot is added or dropped, update matched if that slot's equality flips. The window is an anagram when matched == 26 (or the number of distinct pattern chars).

findings.summary: The mistakes list contains a terse bullet that refers to a technique not explained on the page.
findings.evidence: Not deleting a zero count from a map before comparing
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea in section 3 explaining why zero-count keys break map equality, or say 'compare maps only after removing zero counts'.

findings.summary: The matched-counter idea is stated but not shown as a visual or step list, and the code covers only the longest-without-repeats case.
findings.evidence: Track a matched counter; a slide touches only two slots
findings.fix: Add a small table or steps showing add s[r] / drop s[r-k] updating counts and matched.

findings.summary: The 'Two pointers' row implies an O(n) time, O(1) space way to find the longest palindromic substring, but two pointers only checks whether one string is a palindrome.
findings.evidence: Two pointers | O(n) | O(1), one string
findings.fix: Relabel the row 'Two pointers (palindrome check only) | O(n) | O(1)', or drop it from the alternatives for finding the longest palindromic substring.

findings.summary: The search steps increment i on a match and then record i-m+1, which gives the wrong start index.
findings.evidence: "match: i++, j++" ... "j==m" "record i-m+1"
findings.fix: State that i has already been incremented when j==m, so the match starts at i-m. Alternatively, check j==m before incrementing i, or say the match ends at index i-1.

findings.summary: The search procedure is written as fragmented lines without a table or diagram, so the case-to-action pairing is hard to follow.

Mismatch
j=lps[j-1], keep i
j==m
record i-m+1
Overlap
j=lps[j-1]
findings.fix: Use a two-column table: Case | Action (match, mismatch, j==m).

findings.summary: The code is followed by a stray fragment, and the mistakes list has no heading, so it blends into the search steps.
